IRGC says four vessels carrying oil hit mines near Hormuz, warns US of wider responses
Times of Israel liveblog (Reuters) — 22 October 2026, 7:30 am (Israel time; 05:30 BST)

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy says that four vessels involved in illegal oil transfers in the northern Persian Gulf "were simultaneously hit and caught fire after being tracked by its forces."
The IRGC adds that "three more vessels collided with mines west of the Strait of Hormuz," and warned the US military that continued provocations could lead to a wider response against its regional bases.

(Search snippet content from same entry/aggregated reporting:) The vessels were discovered "transferring oil cargoes from ship to ship in the north-central part of the Persian Gulf," and "all four ships were hit simultaneously and are burning." The IRGC said three other ships attempting to use routes not recognized by Iran "suffered accidents and caught fire after striking mines west of the Strait of Hormuz, and were brought to a halt." The IRGC said the U.S. "encouraging vessels to pass through an illegally mined passage has led to an increasing number of maritime incidents day by day."
